scenario: Autonomous seafloor sensors at hydrothermal vent fields only transmit temperature-spike records when the anomaly exceeds 3.0 °C above ambient. Among transmitted records the mean spike magnitude is 4.5 °C (σ=0.8 °C). Oceanographers need the true mean spike magnitude across all vent-field events.

data.description: Observed statistics among values exceeding the reporting threshold

values.note: Only observations above the threshold enter the record

question: (a) Assuming temperature-spike magnitude follows a normal distribution with σ=0.8 °C, solve numerically for the true population mean μ satisfying E[X | X > 3.0] = 4.5. (b) What fraction of all temperature-spike magnitude events lie above the 3.0 °C threshold? (c) By how much (in °C) does the observed truncated mean overstate the true μ? (d) Explain the inferential risk of using the observed mean directly as an estimate of μ.

ground_truth.explanation: The observed mean 4.5 °C is E[X|X>3.0], the expectation of a truncated-normal distribution. Solving μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=4.5 numerically yields μ=4.43347 °C. Only 96.3% of all events are recorded; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 0.06653 °C. Using the observed mean directly as μ would lead to systematic over-estimation of the severity/magnitude of the process.

naive_answer: The true mean temperature-spike magnitude is 4.5 °C because that is the average of all available measurements.
naive_trap: Only events above 3.0 °C are recorded; the observed mean is a conditional expectation E[X|X>3.0], not the population mean. It always exceeds μ whenever the threshold is binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Define α=(t−μ)/σ where t=3.0, σ=0.8. (2) Truncated-normal expectation: E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 4.5 and solve for μ via brentq on [-17.0, 4.4999]. (4) Solution: μ=4.43347 °C. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=Φ̄((3.0−4.43347)/0.8)=0.96342.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 4.5,0.8,3.0
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-4.43347)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.96342)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-0.06653)<0.01
